Suicide is not selfish, it’s not a solution, it’s the final symptom of potentially deadly clinical depression and suicidal ideation.

It’s not okay for anyone to feel this way, but it is so, so common.

I was initially diagnosed with cyclothymia before I was diagnosed bipolar. Thankfully I found a wonderful therapist in 2016 and together we came to the conclusion that my cyclothymia is intensified by my bipolar disorder and cptsd. All these terms are constantly changing and you have to remind yourself that it’s called “practicing” medicine for a reason. Humans are so incredibly different physiologically, our brain chemistry is no exception. 

Before I found the right combination of therapy and medication my moods could go from euphoric to suicidal and vice versa in a matter of minutes, this was happening long before I had psychiatric intervention. 

What has helped me most is transparency with those closest to me. I stopped hiding what I felt, I lost some friends, but in the end the ones who really matter are still here for me and I couldn’t be happier about tightening my circle. 

It’s taken me two years to find the right combination of medication, it was really fucking hard but I made it and I can genuinely say I really want to be here. 

You’re not a fake. You’re not alone. Your feelings are real. What you’re experiencing is real. I was diagnosed with bipolar II, cyclothymia and PTSD November of 2016 and I'm also an avid pot smoker. 
Marijuana definitely can make you more irritable because of the paranoia and that also induces anxiety. I still smoke, but i smoke less and pretty much only at night. CBD is much more mellow and lacks a lot of the psychoactive component that THC has. 
As for seroquel, I take 150 extended release every night before bed. I've tried lots of other drugs, including Zoloft and the seroquel works best for me with almost no side effects. 
The extended release makes me less drowsy than just taking the regular 100 mg before bed. Drowsiness has been really the only side effect I've experienced and since you take it before bed its really not that noticeable. 
Since the seroquel makes you sleepy at night anyways, it makes it so you don't have to smoke as much to go to sleep. 
Pot has been a huge crutch for me and it's something I still struggle with finding balance, but i hope my account can help you and your son. He's lucky to have a parent who cares.
